item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-37ce54e5f8415b5f","start_unit":4,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"During the June 2023–May 2024 coverage period, Mexico remained an electoral democracy with routine alternation of power, but severe rule-of-law deficits, corruption, human-rights abuses, organized-crime violence, and impunity persisted. The online environment remained a robust space for political mobilization, social discourse, and journalistic investigation, while journalists faced legal threats, harassment, and physical violence that contributed to self-censorship.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.6","3B.8","3B.10","4B.1","4B.3","4B.10","7B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The reporting period overlaps 2023 from June through December and extends into 2024; the source describes conditions relevant to the 2023 ruler-period.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes some online and institutional conditions to the López Obrador administration, while also identifying organized crime and broader structural factors.","limitations":["The source does not establish that López Obrador personally caused all reported violence or self-censorship."]},{"source_id":"SRC-37ce54e5f8415b5f","start_unit":19,"end_unit":23,"fact_summary":"Under López Obrador, autonomous regulators faced government pressure, budget reductions, and delayed commissioner appointments. COFECE obtained commissioners after a Supreme Court order and Senate ratification, but IFT remained short of a full seven-member board through the coverage period; the report considered the failure to fill vacancies detrimental to institutional independence and functioning.","question_ids":["4B.4","4B.5","4B.10","5B.2","5B.4","5B.5","7B.6","8B.4","8B.5"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The evidence includes events before and during 2023, with some later reporting used to describe the continuing institutional condition.","ruler_attribution":"The report directly attributes pressure, budget reductions, and appointment delays to the López Obrador administration, while noting compliance with the Supreme Court order for COFECE appointments.","limitations":["The source does not quantify the operational effect of the budget reductions on every regulator."]},{"source_id":"SRC-37ce54e5f8415b5f","start_unit":34,"end_unit":35,"fact_summary":"Coordinated progovernment online networks reportedly spread narratives and smear campaigns against López Obrador's perceived rivals. In March 2023, pro-AMLO accounts disseminated more than 20,000 messages using unsubstantiated accusations linking Supreme Court president Norma Piña to drug trafficking; a later investigation identified the Red Brolan network spreading progovernment narratives and manipulated or unsubstantiated attacks on opponents and critical journalists, although no evidence showed government or party financing.","question_ids":["3B.3","4B.3","4B.6","6B.8","7B.1","7B.2","7B.8","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The Piña campaign and Red Brolan reporting fall within 2023 or the immediate surrounding coverage period.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the activity to pro-AMLO accounts and an AMLO-friendly network, but expressly states that government or party financing of Red Brolan was not established.","limitations":["Attribution to López Obrador personally or to state financing is not proven for the networks described."]},{"source_id":"SRC-37ce54e5f8415b5f","start_unit":39,"end_unit":42,"fact_summary":"Independent digital media remained vulnerable to public-advertising dependence and alleged government pressure. Article 19 reported that the López Obrador administration failed to deliver an effective state-advertising framework and concentrated official advertising among a small number of outlets; in 2023, 10 media and communication companies received 45.05 percent of the official advertising budget, while 2.559 billion of 2.978 billion pesos appropriated for advertising was spent.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.6","4B.10","5B.5","5B.7","7B.7","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The concentration and spending figures specifically concern 2023, although the evaluative criticism was published in 2024.","ruler_attribution":"The source directly attributes the failure of the advertising framework and concentration of funds to the López Obrador administration.","limitations":["The figures do not by themselves prove that each recipient received funds because of political loyalty or that content was altered."]},{"source_id":"SRC-37ce54e5f8415b5f","start_unit":46,"end_unit":47,"fact_summary":"López Obrador's proposed electoral reforms known as Plan B generated massive demonstrations in February 2023. Social-media users mobilized with anti-reform hashtags, and the Supreme Court invalidated the reforms in May and June 2023 because Congress had not followed proper legislative procedure.","question_ids":["4B.1","4B.2","4B.3","4B.4","4B.8","4B.10","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The demonstrations and Supreme Court rulings occurred in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes Plan B to López Obrador and describes judicial invalidation of the reforms; it also shows that opposition mobilization remained possible.","limitations":["The source does not establish whether the reforms were intended specifically to secure personal continuation in office."]},{"source_id":"SRC-37ce54e5f8415b5f","start_unit":59,"end_unit":63,"fact_summary":"Mexico generally did not restrict anonymity or encryption, but investigators found that government agencies blocked 39 URLs for Tor users between 2020 and October 2023. The military and security agencies were also linked by investigations to Pegasus and other spyware targeting journalists, human-rights defenders, and government investigators; López Obrador denied or minimized the allegations, while authorities were slow to investigate and the use largely remained unpunished. INAI ordered SEDENA to search for and disclose Pegasus contracts in January 2023, but SEDENA did not comply for more than a year.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.7","1B.9","3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","3B.9","4B.3","4B.9","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The evidence includes investigations and institutional actions during 2023, alongside earlier surveillance alleged to continue into the period.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes denials and minimization to López Obrador and links the surveillance operations to military and government agencies, but some individual targeting allegations remain investigative findings rather than final judicial determinations.","limitations":["Some Pegasus attribution was described as alleged or inferential; the source reports limited completed investigations and no final accountability for most cases."]},{"source_id":"SRC-37ce54e5f8415b5f","start_unit":68,"end_unit":71,"fact_summary":"Mexico's telecommunications law required providers to retain metadata for two years and provide real-time geolocation or communications data to authorities under specified conditions. In 2023, Telcel reportedly supplied records of more than a dozen public officials in response to at least 14 Mexico City prosecutor orders without the required judicial authorization. INAI also lacked a quorum from March 2023, although the Supreme Court later allowed it to operate with four commissioners.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.5","4B.4","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The Telcel disclosures and INAI quorum problem are directly relevant to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The legal framework and executive-legislative institutional environment are state-level facts; the source does not prove López Obrador personally ordered the Telcel disclosures.","limitations":["The report says authorities denied requesting the information and does not provide a final adjudication of responsibility for each disclosure."]},{"source_id":"SRC-37ce54e5f8415b5f","start_unit":73,"end_unit":76,"fact_summary":"Article 19 documented 561 attacks on journalists in 2023, including 106 illegitimate uses of public authority, 100 threats, 45 physical attacks, 5 murders potentially related to journalistic work, and 143 digital-sphere attacks. The report also describes murders, disappearances, and threats affecting online journalists, and says López Obrador attempted to discredit journalists; in February 2024 he publicly revealed a New York Times journalist's phone number after criticizing reporting about his political associates.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.3","3B.6","3B.8","3B.9","3B.10","4B.3","7B.1","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The attack statistics specifically concern 2023; the phone-number disclosure occurred in February 2024 and is outside the target year but within the source's coverage period.","ruler_attribution":"The source directly attributes stigmatizing or discrediting conduct to López Obrador and separately records attacks by criminal groups, local officials, and other actors.","limitations":["The source does not establish that López Obrador ordered the physical attacks or murders."]},{"source_id":"SRC-69f444366c0c75ba","start_unit":28,"end_unit":29,"fact_summary":"ARTICLE 19 and partners reported that the Mexican army used Pegasus, despite lacking legal authority for the surveillance, against journalist and human-rights defender Raymundo Ramos after he documented alleged military killings. López Obrador said the report was untrue and characterized the army's activity as intelligence rather than spying.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.7","1B.9","3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","4B.3","4B.9","7B.1","7B.2","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report concerns surveillance disclosed in 2022 and remained materially relevant to López Obrador's 2023 record.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the denial and rhetorical characterization to López Obrador and the surveillance to the Mexican army.","limitations":["The document is an advocacy report and does not provide a final judicial finding against López Obrador personally."]},{"source_id":"SRC-69f444366c0c75ba","start_unit":42,"end_unit":44,"fact_summary":"ARTICLE 19 described deep-rooted corruption and a symbiosis between organized crime and government as continuing to undermine transparency, justice, and accountability in Mexico. It reported persistent stigmatizing discourse by AMLO toward journalists, increased military power in 2022, 37 journalists killed during his presidency through December 2022, 12 journalist murders in Mexico in 2022, and a 97.9 percent impunity rate for crimes against the press. The organization also recorded at least 18 attacks on its Mexico office in 2022 and said authorities failed to investigate or identify perpetrators.","question_ids":["3B.2","3B.3","3B.4","3B.6","3B.8","3B.10","4B.3","7B.6","7B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The quantitative figures concern 2022 but describe the inherited and continuing context entering 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source directly links persistent stigmatizing discourse to AMLO and says he gave the military more power; broader corruption, criminal symbiosis, and attacks have multiple actors.","limitations":["The document does not establish that the administration caused every attack or that all impunity resulted from presidential decisions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-69f444366c0c75ba","start_unit":57,"end_unit":57,"fact_summary":"A Yucatán mayor and five police officers were convicted in 2019 for the 2014 detention and torture of Indigenous journalist Edwin Canché; in 2022 they were ordered to issue a public apology, described as the first such court-ordered apology for violence against the press in Yucatán.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.9","3B.10","4B.3","7B.2","7B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The abuse predates 2023, while the convictions and remedy provide context for institutional accountability entering the target year.","ruler_attribution":"The conduct was attributed to a local mayor and police officers, not López Obrador.","limitations":["The source does not connect the case to federal authorities or the president."]},{"source_id":"SRC-69f444366c0c75ba","start_unit":74,"end_unit":76,"fact_summary":"ARTICLE 19's Mexico office documented and preserved more than 5,000 records of state arrests, torture, disappearances, and killings from 1960–1980 and worked with the Commission for Access to Truth, Historical Clarification, and Justice on historical data and human-rights-informed archives. At the same time, families searching for disappeared relatives in Guanajuato faced aggression and obstruction; ten collectives representing 72 families participated in a 2022 documentation and remembrance project.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.4","3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","4B.3","7B.6","7B.7","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The documentation and commission cooperation occurred in 2022 and provide institutional context relevant to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The source describes civil-society work and a government truth commission, but does not attribute the historical abuses to López Obrador personally.","limitations":["The document does not assess the commission's eventual effectiveness or whether it delivered remedy by the end of 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c0d225ca90a4346a","start_unit":9,"end_unit":11,"fact_summary":"The World Bank described Mexico's government program as targeting vulnerable groups and regions while reforming institutions for sustainable growth. It reported severe inequality and institutional weakness: 43.9 percent multidimensional poverty in 2020, rural household income substantially below urban income, persistent informality, and especially high poverty in southern states. It also identified climate and disaster exposure as disproportionately affecting poor and marginalized populations.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","6B.1","6B.3","6B.6","6B.10","8B.1","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The document was prepared in 2022 and provides baseline and policy context for assessing 2023, not a 2023 outcome measurement.","ruler_attribution":"The stated priorities are those of the López Obrador government, while the poverty and exposure data describe inherited and ongoing structural conditions.","limitations":["Most indicators cited predate 2023 and cannot establish end-of-period outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c0d225ca90a4346a","start_unit":18,"end_unit":20,"fact_summary":"The World Bank reported a cautious countercyclical fiscal response, increased health and social-assistance spending, and public investment, while noting substantial support to loss-making PEMEX: cumulative government support of 2.7 percent of 2021 GDP during 2019–2021, with PEMEX debt of about MXN 2.243 trillion at end-2021. The 2022 budget aimed to stabilize debt and deficits, but revenue-stabilization funds had been heavily depleted and PEMEX remained a fiscal risk.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.6","5B.9","5B.10","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The evidence concerns 2019–2022 and forecasts 2023; it is contextual rather than a direct 2023 execution finding.","ruler_attribution":"The fiscal choices and PEMEX support are attributed to the government during López Obrador's administration.","limitations":["The document's 2023 figures are projections made in 2022, not observed 2023 outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c0d225ca90a4346a","start_unit":26,"end_unit":29,"fact_summary":"The government enacted a simplified income-tax regime for MSMEs and self-employed workers, adding tax-authority tools against evasion and reducing filing procedures. The reform was designed to be revenue-neutral in the short term and potentially increase formalization, but the World Bank noted uncertainty, possible incentives for firms to remain small, and neutral expected poverty and social effects. The operation also supported remote bank-account opening for Mexican migrants and digital-payment regulations covering consumer protection and cybersecurity.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.4","5B.7","5B.8","5B.10","6B.1","6B.2","6B.3","6B.5","6B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6","8B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The legal actions were adopted in 2021–2022, with results targets for December 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The reforms were government measures supported by the López Obrador administration and implemented through SHCP and financial regulators.","limitations":["The source reports intended results and risks, not verified achievement of the 2023 targets."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c0d225ca90a4346a","start_unit":34,"end_unit":39,"fact_summary":"The government established budgetary mechanisms and risk-transfer provisions for post-disaster response, amended the Forest Law to require mitigation of lost carbon storage, prohibit land-use authorization on recently deforested land, and require free, prior, and informed consultation in Indigenous territories. It also declared the Sierra de San Miguelito protected area, covering 111,160 hectares and securing an estimated 89,362 hectares of ecosystems storing about 1.1 million tons of carbon. The World Bank identified positive environmental and resilience objectives but noted implementation and distributional risks.","question_ids":["1B.9","3B.7","3B.9","3B.10","5B.1","5B.6","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","6B.3","6B.6","6B.8","6B.9","6B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7","8B.10"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"The legal reforms and protected-area decree were adopted in 2021, with implementation and results targets extending to 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The measures were enacted by the López Obrador government through SHCP, SEMARNAT, and presidential decree.","limitations":["The document does not verify full implementation or realized 2023 outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c0d225ca90a4346a","start_unit":45,"end_unit":46,"fact_summary":"A November 2021 presidential accord declared certain infrastructure projects matters of national security and public interest and ordered provisional environmental and social permits within five business days. The Supreme Court partially suspended the accord after an INAI challenge; SEMARNAT said it had not yet been implemented and continued applying the environmental framework, but the World Bank judged potential implementation a significant risk to environmental safeguards and reform outcomes.","question_ids":["1B.9","3B.4","3B.9","4B.4","4B.9","5B.4","5B.6","5B.7","5B.10","7B.6","7B.7","8B.8","8B.9","8B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The accord and litigation predate 2023 but were identified as an ongoing implementation risk for the period.","ruler_attribution":"The accord was issued by López Obrador as president.","limitations":["The source states the accord had not been implemented as of the document's preparation; it therefore shows exposure and institutional conflict more than realized harm."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c0d225ca90a4346a","start_unit":47,"end_unit":49,"fact_summary":"The World Bank noted that Mexico's disaster-response budget covered only an average or below-average loss year and that a disaster comparable to the 2017 earthquake could exceed the 2022 budget. It nevertheless assessed the new provisions as potentially improving timely resource deployment, especially for vulnerable southern states, and proposed monitoring through technically supported risk-financing instruments.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.9","3B.9","3B.10","5B.9","6B.6","6B.10","8B.3","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"The assessment concerns the 2022 framework and its expected operation through 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The provisions were adopted by Mexico's executive financial authorities during López Obrador's administration.","limitations":["No actual 2023 disaster-response test or outcome is supplied."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":[],"batch_limitations":["The supplied Freedom House document primarily covers June 1, 2023–May 31, 2024, and the supplied World Bank document was prepared in 2022 with 2023 projections; period fit is therefore explicitly qualified where evidence is not a direct 2023 observation.","The supplied Article 19 annual report concerns 2022 and is used only for inherited or continuing conditions relevant to the 2023 period.","Facts are limited to the supplied documents; no scores or chapter judgments are provided."]}
